picks.thesis: Convergence, but with legs of different vintage. Three House members bought TSM in Jan-Feb 2026, including Gilbert Cisneros twice and a $100,001-250,000 band on 2026-02-09 (C-17f8c4c8bcd3); that leg is roughly six months stale. The fresh leg is insider: nineteen named officers, including Chairman and CEO Wei Che-Chia, disclosed open-market buys dated 2026-07-07 through 2026-08-07 and filed within three days, none flagged 10b5-1. Breadth is the signal; size is not - disclosed amounts run 513 to 11,143, and the near-uniform same-day pattern on 2026-08-07 argues against reading each as an independent decision. TSM closed 420.04 on 2026-08-07, down 3.87% over 30 days and below its 90-day high of 477.57.
key_risks: The congressional leg is roughly six months old; disclosure bands are ranges, and one buy could be anywhere from $100,001 to $250,000.
Nineteen officer buys clustered on a single date at small, similar amounts may reflect a routine company mechanism rather than nineteen independent views.
Cisneros sits on House Armed Services, a committee with defense-semiconductor oversight exposure - that raises the stakes and is also why such trades attract scrutiny.
The price is down 3.87% over 30 days, so the fresh insider buying has not yet coincided with a rising tape.
picks.invalidation: The August officer buying stops appearing in subsequent Form 4s, or the same officers begin filing sales, while TSM trades back toward the 90-day low of 374.67.

expression.defined_risk_note: Information only: a view resting on breadth of insider buying but stale congressional evidence is the kind that is sometimes expressed through a defined-risk structure such as a long call spread, where the maximum loss is the premium paid rather than the position value.

picks.thesis: A persistent single-filer accumulation, not a cluster. April McClain Delaney disclosed twelve HUBB buys between 2026-05-13 and 2026-07-23, ten in the $1,001-15,000 band and two at $15,001-50,000, the most recent on 2026-07-23 with an eleven-day filing lag. She sits on House Science, Space, and Technology, which the engine maps to this name's tech sector tag - alignment that raises the stakes and is also why such trades draw scrutiny. No insider Form 4 buying corroborates it, and every evidence record traces to one person, so the case rests on repetition alone. HUBB closed 513.99 on 2026-08-07, up 8.77% in five days and below its 90-day high of 539.39.
key_risks: One filer. There is no second congressional buyer and no insider Form 4 buying in the data to confirm the read.
Every buy sits in a small band; twelve filings in the $1,001-50,000 range may reflect routine portfolio activity rather than conviction.
Filing lags run from 7 to 34 days, so the earlier purchases were reported well after the fact.
The stock has already run 8.77% in five days, so the disclosed buys precede a move that has partly occurred.
picks.invalidation: Delaney's next disclosures show HUBB sales, or the buying simply stops while the price falls back toward the 90-day low of 459.5988.

expression.defined_risk_note: Information only: single-filer evidence of this weight is more often held as a watchlist item than a position; if expressed at all, defined-risk structures cap the loss at premium rather than at position value.
